statement: BEST (displayed PERSISTENT) does not beat a scored-pile random pick on the MEDIAN 6h net return at $500. Expected null: an out-of-sample replication of the pre-log backtest, where BEST led WATCH by 0.19pp pooled and trailed it by 1.30pp clustered by token, with the sign flipping across three consecutive weeks.
population: label rows with tier == 'BEST' and ts > log_watermark, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly
metric: MEDIAN(ret_net_500) of the population minus MEDIAN of the per-row same-pile baseline medians. Median, not mean: the distributions are long-tailed and a mean is a different claim.
baseline: pile=scored, 20 draws, seeded sha256(ts|ca|scored), computed at summary time
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met, the gap is below +1.0pp -- the null stands, BEST does not beat a random traded token
fail_if: the gap is at or above +1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods -- the null is false and BEST carries forward information
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or above +1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 weekly subperiods -- the size is there and the stability is not, which is exactly the shape the earlier finding had and is not a result either way
notes: min_eff_n counts distinct (ca, 6h-bucket) cells, not rows: at 15-minute sampling a 6h horizon overlaps ~24x, and on the synthetic replay 6,418 thinned rows collapsed to 1,223 cells. 300 cells is about 7 days at the observed ~56 BEST cells/day. pile MUST be scored: a tier drawn against its own members cannot test whether the tier is any good.

statement: A higher recent_move_score is followed by worse 6h returns. Out-of-sample replication of the mean-reversion finding, where _band(chg_h6) at +5 preceded a -3.96% median gross 4-8h return against -0.69% at -5, surviving pairing, clustering and a retention control but NOT the regime split.
population: label rows with ts > log_watermark, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly, split into rms >= +4 and rms <= -4
baseline: not used -- a within-population contrast, and both arms carry the same modelled costs
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met in BOTH arms, the gap is at or below -1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods
fail_if: the gap is above -1.0pp once min_eff_n is met in both arms
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or below -1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 subperiods -- the original effect was +0.06pp in week 38 against -1.13 and -1.44pp in weeks 39 and 40, so this outcome means the regime dependence reproduced rather than the effect
notes: min_eff_n is per arm. The horizon narrows: the labeler's 6h +/-45min is [5.25h, 6.75h], inside the original 4-8h window rather than matching it. That is deliberate, and it means a null here does not fully refute the original.

statement: EMERGING is lottery-shaped at 6h: a median materially worse than a random traded token, with a mean above its own median, meaning a few large winners against many losers. In the pre-log backtest the 4-8h median was -7.46% against a mean of +1.55% across 111 tokens, negative on 11 of 15 days.
population: label rows with tier == 'EMERGING' and ts > log_watermark, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly
metric: three jointly: (a) MEDIAN(ret_net_500); (b) MEDIAN(ret_net_500) minus the median same-pile baseline; (c) MEAN(ret_net_500) minus MEDIAN(ret_net_500)
baseline: pile=scored, 20 draws, seeded sha256(ts|ca|scored), computed at summary time
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met, ALL THREE hold: (a) median at or below -5.0pp, (b) at least 3.0pp below the scored baseline's median, (c) mean exceeds median by at least 5.0pp
fail_if: any of the three fails once min_eff_n is met
inconclusive_if: min_eff_n is met but censoring exceeds max_censored_pct -- EMERGING tokens are young and drop out, and a median over a half-censored population is not the claim
notes: The bare claim 'EMERGING has a negative median 6h net return' is near-trivially true and would not have been worth registering: modelled costs are 2% in fees plus impact, so the scored baseline's own median is about -4.2pp and almost every population is negative after costs. Clause (b) makes it a claim about EMERGING rather than about the cost model; clause (c) makes it a claim about shape rather than level. max_censored_pct is 50 rather than 20 because the pre-log 24h censoring was 45.4%, and a tighter bar would expire this for a reason that is itself the finding.

statement: Tokens whose surviving top-10 holders hold an unusually large share of the holders we can see do WORSE on the 6h median net return than the rest of the same snapshot's scored pile. Registered before any holder data exists, against a folk claim -- that concentrated holdings precede dumps -- which this project has never tested on this chain. No prior from this repo supports or contradicts it.
uses: holder concentration from data/holders/, not any tier or score
population: label rows with ts > log_watermark whose ca appears in the nearest holders snapshot within 90 minutes, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly, split into the top quartile of conc10 within each holders snapshot and the rest of that same snapshot
metric: conc10 = (sum of the balances of the 10 largest SURVIVING holders) / (sum of the balances of ALL surviving holders in that snapshot's stored top 20). A holder survives exclusion unless it is is_contract true, the token contract itself, the token's main_pool, a burn address (0x0...0, 0x...dEaD), or listed in data/holders/exclusions_hint.json as of the evaluation run. Denominator is the stored top 20, NOT total_supply: supply is null for all but the five stock tokens, and a metric that silently changes definition with coverage is not one metric. The reported figure is MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | top quartile) minus MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | rest), in percentage points.
baseline: not used -- a within-snapshot contrast, and both arms carry the same modelled costs, so the fee term cancels in the difference
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met in BOTH arms, the gap is at or below -1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods
fail_if: the gap is above -1.0pp once min_eff_n is met in both arms
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or below -1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 weekly subperiods; or fewer than 60% of the population's rows find a holders snapshot inside the 90-minute join window, which would make the quartile a statement about coverage rather than about concentration
notes: THRESHOLD IS RELATIVE. The split is the top quartile of conc10 WITHIN each holders snapshot, so no absolute concentration cutoff is chosen after seeing the distribution, and the arms stay balanced as the board turns over. min_eff_n is per arm and counts distinct (ca, 6h-bucket) cells, as in H-0001. stop_by is later than H-0001..3 because the holders log starts from zero rows and 8 snapshots a day is a slower accrual than the 15-minute pool log. NOT YET BUILT, deliberately: nothing joins holders to labels today. evaluate.py would need (a) a loader for data/holders/*/*.jsonl, (b) an as-of join on (ca, nearest ts within 90 minutes, never forward in time), (c) the exclusion filter above applied at evaluation rather than at collection, and (d) the per-snapshot quartile split; label.py needs no change, since ret_net_500 is already what it emits. Writing that join before the data exists would mean tuning it against nothing.

statement: Tokens whose top 10 surviving holders hold an unusually large share of TOTAL SUPPLY do WORSE on the 6h median net return than the rest of the same snapshot's pile. Successor to H-0004, which asked the same question against the wrong denominator. No outcome data has ever been joined to holder data, by H-0004 or anything else.
uses: holder concentration from data/holders/, not any tier or score
population: label rows with ts > log_watermark whose ca appears in a holders snapshot at or before the entry time and within 3.5 hours of it, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly, split into the top quartile of conc10 within each holders snapshot and the rest of that same snapshot
metric: conc10 = (sum of the balances of the 10 largest SURVIVING holders) / total_supply, both raw integers in base units so decimals cancels. A holder survives unless it is a burn address (0x0...0 or an address ending 0x...dead), the token contract itself, a pool contract (the row's main_pool, or is_contract true with a pool-shaped label), or listed in data/holders/exclusions_hint.json as of the evaluation run. Rows with a null total_supply are dropped from the population, not imputed. The reported figure is MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | top quartile) minus MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | rest), in percentage points.
baseline: not used -- a within-snapshot contrast, and both arms carry the same modelled costs, so the fee term cancels in the difference
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met in BOTH arms, the gap is at or below -1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods
fail_if: the gap is above -1.0pp once min_eff_n is met in both arms
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or below -1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 weekly subperiods; or fewer than 60% of the population's rows find a holders snapshot inside the 3.5-hour join window; or more than 25% of the top arm entered it on a tie-break, which would make the split a statement about ties rather than about concentration
notes: WHY THIS SUPERSEDES H-0004, and when the change was made. H-0004's denominator was the stored top 20 rather than total supply, because at registration no supply was available for 114 of 119 tokens. The first holders run (2026-10-19T15:34Z, 119 tokens) showed that denominator is degenerate: 63% of tokens have 10 or fewer surviving holders, so conc10 is exactly 1.0 for them and the top-quartile cutoff falls inside a tie block of 63 tokens out of 100. The split would have measured how few holders Blockscout returns, not concentration. The same run also showed the 90-minute join window was wrong for a 3-hour cadence: at best a third of label rows could find a snapshot in it. THE CHANGE WAS MADE AFTER SEEING THE PREDICTOR'S DISTRIBUTION AND THE COVERAGE ARITHMETIC, AND BEFORE ANY OUTCOME DATA EXISTED. No return was ever joined to a holder row, so no clause here was chosen to make a result come out. That is the distinction this registry rests on and it is recorded rather than assumed. TIE-BREAK: within a snapshot, order by conc10 descending, then by total_supply descending, then by ca ascending; the top quartile is the first ceil(n/4) of that order. Deterministic, and independent of file order. The report must state how many of the top arm were decided by the second or third key. JOIN WINDOW: 3.5 hours, as-of and never forward in time, so a 3-hourly snapshot can always serve the label rows that follow it without a gap. NOT YET BUILT: see BACKLOG.md; the evaluator join is deliberately deferred until there are snapshots to join against.

statement: Tokens whose top 10 surviving holders hold an unusually large share of TOTAL SUPPLY do WORSE on the 6h median net return than the rest of the same snapshot's pile. Successor to H-0005, which asked exactly this question but could never be evaluated: it carried no log watermark, and its exclusion set was read from a file that changes every run. No outcome data has ever been joined to holder data, by H-0004, H-0005 or anything else.
uses: holder concentration from data/holders/, not any tier or score
population: label rows with ts > log_watermark whose ca appears in a holders snapshot at or before the entry time and within 3.5 hours of it, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly, split into the top quartile of conc10 within each holders snapshot and the rest of that same snapshot. COVERAGE FLOOR: a holders snapshot counts only if its sidecar (data/holders/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS.meta.json) reports coverage >= 0.90; a snapshot below that floor, or one with no sidecar at all, is treated as never collected. A label row then uses the nearest EARLIER counted snapshot within the 3.5-hour window, never a forward one; if there is no counted snapshot in the window the row is dropped from the population and counts toward the 60% join-coverage clause in inconclusive_if.

A holder survives unless it is (a) a burn address -- 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000, or any address whose last four hex characters are dead -- (b) the token contract itself, (c) the row's main_pool, or (d) one of exactly two fixed infrastructure addresses: 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 (Uniswap v4 PoolManager) and 0x267444d099b10fb5ed7c3cc7b7c767adca574952 (PonsV2LaunchLocker). That list is CLOSED and is part of this registration: data/holders/exclusions_hint.json is NOT read at evaluation time, and no address may be added to the exclusion set without registering a new hypothesis. Rows with a null total_supply are dropped from the population, not imputed. The reported figure is MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | top quartile) minus MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | rest), in percentage points.
baseline: not used -- a within-snapshot contrast, and both arms carry the same modelled costs, so the fee term cancels in the difference
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met in BOTH arms, the gap is at or below -1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods
fail_if: the gap is above -1.0pp once min_eff_n is met in both arms
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or below -1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 weekly subperiods; or fewer than 60% of the population's rows find a holders snapshot inside the 3.5-hour join window; or more than 25% of the top arm entered it on a tie-break, which would make the split a statement about ties rather than about concentration; or fewer than 3 counted snapshots fall in any weekly subperiod used for the sign test, since a sign computed from one or two cross-sections is a statement about those cross-sections rather than about the week
notes: WHY THIS SUPERSEDES H-0005, and when the change was made. Three reasons, every one of them visible before any outcome data existed. (1) H-0005 was registered with log_watermark null, which is how a hypothesis waits for data that does not exist yet. Nothing could ever be evaluated against it: scripts/evaluate.py reports it as 'not started' and computes no population at all. This line carries a real watermark, so H-0006 is the first holder-concentration hypothesis that can actually be run. (2) H-0005's exclusion rule read data/holders/exclusions_hint.json 'as of the evaluation run', and that file changes every run. It has held 2 or 3 addresses across the seven runs so far, and 0x2be87ad70cf11ea294d7c42044b5b8277a3e4874 entered it exactly once -- at the 2026-10-19T22:10Z run, in 10 tokens -- then left again, because its per-run count of tokens where it is a top-3 holder went 3, 2, 10, 4, 3, 0, 0 against a threshold of 5. An exclusion set that moves means the same evaluation on two different days is two different tests, which is the one thing a pre-registered metric may not be. H-0006 fixes the set in this line instead, and the hint file reverts to what it was always labelled as: a report. (3) The 2026-10-20 Blockscout outage degraded three consecutive runs -- coverage 0.8922 at 01:10, 0.8182 at 04:10 and 0.7544 at 07:10, against 1.0 at 10:10 -- and the dropped tokens are not a random sample. Across all seven snapshots the tokens that gapped had a mean liquidity rank of 36 against the board's 53, and 89% of them sat at the 20-holder cap against 62% of the board, because a holders page that must return 20 rows is a heavier query than one returning 3. A thin cross-section is therefore thin in exactly the arm this metric is about. Hence the 0.90 coverage floor. Note that 0.8922 for the 01:10 run is a CONSERVATIVE LOWER BOUND rather than an exact figure: that run did not record which tokens failed as against which returned no holders, so its sidecar reports written/planned with coverage_bound 'lower'. It is excluded by the floor either way, and excluding it is the safe direction. THE CHANGE WAS MADE AFTER SEEING COVERAGE AND HINT FLICKER, AND BEFORE ANY OUTCOME DATA WAS EVER JOINED TO A HOLDER ROW. That is not an assumption: scripts/evaluate.py implements rules for H-0001, H-0002 and H-0003 only, and data/holders/ is read by nothing in this repository -- not the dashboard, not label.py, not build_db.py. No return has ever been joined to a holder row by H-0004, by H-0005 or by anything else, so no clause here was chosen to make a result come out. That is the distinction this registry rests on and it is recorded rather than assumed. TIE-BREAK: within a snapshot, order by conc10 descending, then by total_supply descending, then by ca ascending; the top quartile is the first ceil(n/4) of that order. Deterministic, and independent of file order. The report must state how many of the top arm were decided by the second or third key. JOIN WINDOW: 3.5 hours, as-of and never forward in time, so a 3-hourly snapshot can always serve the label rows that follow it without a gap. NOT YET BUILT: see docs/TECH_NOTES.md; the evaluator join is deliberately deferred until there are counted snapshots to join against.

statement: Tokens whose top 10 surviving holders hold an unusually large share of TOTAL SUPPLY do WORSE on the 6h median net return than the rest of the same snapshot's pile. Successor to H-0006, which asks the same question but counts the token's own non-main liquidity pools as holders. No outcome data has ever been joined to holder data, by H-0004, H-0005, H-0006 or anything else.
uses: holder concentration from data/holders/ and data/holders/contract_probe.json, not any tier or score
population: label rows with ts > log_watermark whose ca appears in a holders snapshot at or before the entry time and within 3.5 hours of it, 6h entry snapshots thinned hourly, split into the top quartile of conc10 within each holders snapshot and the rest of that same snapshot. COVERAGE FLOOR: a holders snapshot counts only if its sidecar (data/holders/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS.meta.json) reports coverage >= 0.90; a snapshot below that floor, or with no sidecar, is treated as never collected. A label row uses the nearest EARLIER counted snapshot within the 3.5-hour window, never a forward one. PROBE COMPLETENESS: a holders row counts only if every holder in its stored top 20 that has is_contract true and is not removed by rules (a) to (d) below has a settled result ('ok' or 'revert') in data/holders/contract_probe.json at the pinned evaluation commit; 'error' and absent count as unsettled. SUPPLY SANITY: a holders row counts only if total_supply is a JSON string of decimal digits greater than zero (base units); a null, a number, or anything else drops the row. A holders row that fails PROBE COMPLETENESS or SUPPLY SANITY is dropped from its snapshot BEFORE the quartile split, and every label row that would have joined it is dropped from the population and counts toward the 60% join-coverage clause in inconclusive_if.
metric: conc10 = (sum of the balances of the 10 largest SURVIVING holders) / total_supply, both raw integers in base units so decimals cancels. A holder survives unless it is (a) a burn address: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000, or any address whose last four hex characters are dead; (b) the token contract itself; (c) the row's main_pool; (d) one of exactly two fixed infrastructure addresses: 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 (Uniswap v4 PoolManager) and 0x267444d099b10fb5ed7c3cc7b7c767adca574952 (PonsV2LaunchLocker); (e) A POOL OF THIS TOKEN: its contract_probe.json entry has result 'ok' and its token0 or token1, compared lower-case, equals the row's ca; (f) a holder with is_contract true whose label, compared exactly and case-sensitively, is one of: RehypeDopplerHookInitializer, DopplerHookInitializer, PonsV2BondingCurve, PonsV2MemeHook, StandardLaunchFactory, DLMM Token, Morpho, TibbirBridgeRobinhood -- launch infrastructure (curves, hooks, launch factories, a liquidity-book pair) and pooled custody of many users' tokens (a lending market, a bridge escrow), which hold the token for the market rather than for a holder. The address list in (d) and the label list in (f) are CLOSED and part of this registration: data/holders/exclusions_hint.json is NOT read, and nothing may be added to either list without registering a new hypothesis. Every other holder survives, including contracts that reverted the probe with no label or any other label (SafeProxy, GnosisSafeProxy, lockers, vesting, staking, VotingEscrow, PonsV2FeeEscrow, PonsV2BuybackVault, timelocks): those can be insider-controlled and are real concentration. A holders row whose conc10 exceeds 1.0 is dropped as a units error and counted under the 60% clause. The reported figure is MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | top quartile) minus MEDIAN(ret_net_500 | rest), in percentage points.
baseline: not used -- a within-snapshot contrast, and both arms carry the same modelled costs, so the fee term cancels in the difference
pass_if: after min_eff_n is met in BOTH arms, the gap is at or below -1.0pp AND holds that sign in at least 3 of 4 weekly subperiods
fail_if: the gap is above -1.0pp once min_eff_n is met in both arms
inconclusive_if: the gap is at or below -1.0pp but the sign holds in fewer than 3 of 4 weekly subperiods; or fewer than 60% of the population's rows find a counted, probe-complete, supply-sane holders row inside the 3.5-hour join window; or more than 25% of the top arm entered it on a tie-break; or fewer than 3 counted snapshots fall in any weekly subperiod used for the sign test
notes: WHY THIS SUPERSEDES H-0006, and when. H-0006's exclusions remove only the row's main_pool, so a token's other pools (a second v3 pool, a v2 pair, a CL pool on another DEX) count as holders. 69% of main-pool holder entries carry no Blockscout label, so a label rule alone cannot find pools; a structural test can. holders.py (HS-73, from 984b6fab) asks every non-fixed contract holder token0() then token1() once and caches the raw answer. Rule (e) uses that answer. Rule (f) handles launch infrastructure that holds the token for the market but does not answer token0(): bonding curves, launch hooks, and pools whose interface is not token0/token1. THE CHANGE WAS MADE AFTER SEEING THE PREDICTOR SIDE ONLY: holder labels, probe results and conc10 distributions in the counted snapshots up to registration. No return has ever been joined to a holder row: scripts/evaluate.py implements H-0001..H-0003 only and nothing in the repo reads data/holders/ for outcomes. WHAT THE PRE-REGISTRATION LOOK FOUND (counted snapshots, Claude chat, 2026-10-21): rule (e) removes 606 top-10 entries across 1,541 rows, 138 of them unlabelled; no contract answered token0() for a pair that does not include the row's token. Stock-token rows store total_supply as a float in whole units, which makes conc10 meaningless; SUPPLY SANITY drops them. KNOWN LIMITATION, stated before any outcome: unlabelled contracts that revert the probe still count. One launch EOA (0xbdaffd92390423a70fec81bce3ce213011b08024, through three factories) leaves a token-specific unlabelled contract holding about 55% of supply, very likely its curve or vault. In the snapshots seen, unlabelled contracts were at least half of conc10 in 18% of top-arm rows and 27% of the rest. The report must print, for each arm, the share of rows where unlabelled contracts are at least half of conc10; it does not decide. Cached total_supply never refreshes, so a mintable token's supply can go stale; the conc10 > 1.0 drop catches only the extreme case. DECIDED BY PETE 2026-10-21 before registration: the rule (f) list above (launch infrastructure and pooled custody excluded; team-side escrows and vaults, Safes, lockers, vesting and staking counted), and the launchpad limitation handled as report-only rather than by a collector change. PonsV2LaunchLocker stays in (d) as inherited from H-0006. THE PROBE CACHE IS READ AT THE PINNED EVALUATION COMMIT. A settled result never changes, so a later commit can only add rows, never reclassify one. FREEZE: once the evaluator join for H-0007 exists, nothing here may change without a new counted hypothesis. This is the last free supersession of the holders question. TIE-BREAK and JOIN WINDOW as in H-0006: order by conc10 descending, then total_supply descending, then ca ascending; top quartile = first ceil(n/4); report how many entered on the second or third key.
